title: The collapse time of weak measurement on $N$ entangled sites
authors: Truong-Son P. Van, David W. Snoke
abstract: We determine the time required for local weak measurements to collapse to one occupied site in an initial superposition of $N$ alternatives in the model of PRA 111, 032217 (2025). For equal initial occupation probabilities and a fixed confidence threshold $1-δ$, we prove $T_N/\ln N\to1/2$ in $L^1$, with time measured in units of the characteristic measurement time $τ_m$ of each detector. We also connect the asymptotic stabilization theorem of that work to a finite measurement: the first site to reach $1-δ$ is the eventual outcome with conditional probability exactly $1-δ$. The result corrects the previously proposed double-logarithmic asymptotic scaling. The finite-range numerical fit does not determine a constant asymptotic correction or a precise finite-$N$ law.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the time required for weak measurements to collapse an initial superposition of $N$ quantum states down to a single outcome. It rigorously proves that this collapse time scales linearly with $\ln N$, correcting previous theoretical estimates. The results are significant for understanding the dynamics of measurement back-action in entangled quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the time scale required for local weak measurements to collapse the occupation probability of an initial superposition of $N$ alternatives down to a single occupied site.
main_result: The collapse time $T_N$ scales asymptotically as $T_N / \ln N 	o 1/2$ in $L^1$, correcting previous estimates of double-logarithmic scaling.
method: The analysis uses stochastic differential equations for the occupation weights, martingale theory, and bounding techniques derived from information theory (entropy).
model_or_system: The system models a single excitation initially superposed equally among $N$ entangled sites, where local weak measurements continuously monitor the occupation probability of each site.
key_observables: Collapse time $T_N$, occupation probabilities $w_n(t)$, and the system entropy $H(t)$.
important_parameters: The number of sites $N$, the confidence threshold $\delta$, and the characteristic measurement time $	au_m$.
main_assumptions: The initial occupation probabilities are assumed to be equal ($1/N$), and the analysis relies on the weights being bounded martingales.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares simulated Gaussian means against theoretical curves, showing the proposed logarithmic fit has a significantly lower Root-Mean-Square Deviation than previously published double-logarithmic curves.
paper_structure: The paper develops the evolution equations for the weights, establishes bounds on the collapse time using martingale theory, proves the asymptotic scaling law, and finally addresses the reliability of the first crossing event.
why_interesting: This work provides precise scaling laws for measurement-induced collapse in entangled quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding measurement back-action in quantum computation and quantum sensing.
